title: SDK instrumentation quality gates and Console feedback loop for propagation correctness
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Ship a set of SDK-level instrumentation quality gates combined with Console-visible feedback that detects propagation regressions, sampling misalignment, and dropped spans early in PRs and production canaries. The feature should enable engineering teams to catch context-loss and sampling-configuration bugs before they impact customer SLAs and make it easy to see when the SDK/middleware chain is the root cause.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK exposes an opt-in 'propagation-evaluator' hook that can be enabled at initialization and emits a lightweight verification span for sampled and unsampled requests. 2) Console receives a new 'propagation-check' metric stream with per-route counts: verified, failed, soft-fail (degraded propagation), and injected-checks. 3) CI check (via GH action) runs the evaluator fuzz tests on PRs touching SDK or middleware layers and fails on >0 regressions. 4) Rollout plan implements a 10% canary for 48h with automated rollback if propagation-failure rate exceeds 0.5% or error rate increases >2x baseline. 5) Documentation and PRD links included; SDK changelog and migration guide published. 6) Telemetry dashboards in Console show propagation quality over time and link to offending traces.
implementation_notes: High-level approach: implement an evaluation shim in the core SDKs (Node, Python, Go) that registers a thin middleware/hook layer. On active evaluation runs the shim appends a deterministically named verification span and a short JSON payload in baggage that includes a monotonic check-sum of header values and sampling decision. The verification span is marked as 'meta.propagation_check'. To avoid noise and cost: evaluator emits only for a configurable sampling fraction (default 0.02) and has a separate 'force' mode for CI and smoke tests. The shim is resilient to missing headers: it records a 'soft-fail' instead of blowing up the request path. Server-side ingestion: runtime telemetry adapters must map the verification span into metrics and short tag sets (route, model, sdk_version, env). This mapping will be handled via a new lightweight processor in the telemetry pipeline (see pipeline PR). Backward compatibility: evaluator uses feature flags so customers can opt into auto-instrumentation without changing request payloads. All verification baggage keys are namespaced under 'rwd:' to avoid collision.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for shim logic and baggage checksum calculation. 2) Fuzz harness that mutates header order, splits headers across network boundaries, and simulates sampled/unsampled decisions. 3) Integration tests: Node + edge-proxy + runtime locally that assert detection of propagation loss. 4) GH action that runs fuzz harness on PRs. 5) Canary in staging and then prod: watch propagation-check metric and related error/latency SLIs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): merge SDK PRs behind feature flag; enable in internal staging. Phase 2 (canary): 10% traffic for 48h on low-risk routes; automated alerting if failures >0.5% or latency regresses. Phase 3 (gradual): ramp to 100% over 7 days after manual review. Phase 4: enable CI checks org-wide and publish migration guide.
monitoring_and_alerting: New Console dashboard: 'Propagation Health' showing per-route heatmap and time-series for verified / failed / soft-fail rates. Alert rules: P0 alert for >0.5% failed propagation across top 10 routes or any spike in propagation-related errors. Secondary alerts for mismatch between sampling decision and presence of verification span (indicates sampler misalignment).
